diagnosis.root_cause: Intermittent degradation on this subscriber's optical path, causing RX power to fluctuate between degraded and critical levels and producing signal-driven session flapping. The ONU laser and OLT are healthy.
evidence: The subscriber has 16 sessions in 24 hours, well above the normal 2-3 and above the 8+ flapping threshold; average session duration is only 71 minutes versus the 11.9-hour baseline.
Current RX power is -27.94 dBm live and -26.28 dBm in stored state, which is degraded and close to or periodically within the critical range.

The seven-day RX series repeatedly swings by several dBm, from approximately -24.2 to below -28.5 dBm. This is far wider than the healthy +/-0.3 dBm noise floor and indicates a real intermittent optical-path change.
TX power remains stable around 2.3 dBm and TX bias current remains around 11 mA within the healthy range, ruling against laser degradation.
Distance remains constant at 302 m, ruling against a fibre path or ONU reassignment event.
The ONU is currently online, authenticated, responding, and completing exchange, so this is not a persistent ONU-offline condition.

Other ONUs on EPON0/2 have substantially better and stable RX levels, while all PONs and OLT metrics are healthy; this localizes the fault to the single customer's fibre path rather than the PON port, splitter, OLT, or router.
VLAN 1092, RADIUS records, line ID, assigned IP, and CRM data are consistent, so provisioning and authentication faults are not supported.

remediation.action: Dispatch field service to inspect and clean/reterminate the subscriber drop, connectors, patch points, and splice path; perform an OTDR and optical power test for excessive loss or reflection. Repair or replace the defective fibre segment or connector, then verify RX power is stable in the normal range and confirm session frequency returns to baseline.

ground_truth.root_cause: RX power oscillates between roughly -24.4 and -28.2 dBm on an eleven hour cycle, crossing the threshold at which the link stops being usable. The session drops follow the signal excursions.
expected_reasoning: Sixteen sessions in 24 hours against a 2-3 baseline, with a 71 minute mean duration
Cached RX is -26.28 dBm, already in the degraded band
Telemetry shows RX oscillating between about -24.4 and -28.2 dBm on an eleven hour cycle
The lower excursions cross -28 dBm, at which point the link becomes unusable
Live RX of -27.94 confirms the signal is currently near the bottom of that swing
TX power, bias current, supply voltage and distance are all stable, so the ONU is healthy
RADIUS is clean with a single consistent entry and no mismatches
Peers on EPON0/2 read normal, so the fault is in this customer's own path
The session pattern tracks the signal excursions, so the optical fault explains the flapping
distractors: The trigger names the session count, pointing at the auth layer
Sixteen disconnects is well within the observed flapping tail and could be read as a CPE fault
